psat-a:
You are writing PSAT/NMSQT practice for one strong student, at the level of the hard second module. Read {GEN}/SPEC-psat.md in full — it is the brief: who the student is (790 Math, 730 Reading and Writing on the September SAT, aiming at a 228 Selection Index on the October PSAT/NMSQT), the format you imitate, the file shapes and the checks. Read the math house style in {GEN}/SPEC.md ("Exclusions, borrowing, style": the Unicode-first rule and the only TeX allowed) and the checker {GEN}/tests.py (check_psat).

Your tests: "conv" (20 questions: Boundaries and Form, structure, and sense, at least 3 of each, 24 minutes), "expr" (20 questions: Transitions and Rhetorical synthesis, 24 minutes), and "rw1" (a full 27-question hard Reading and Writing module, 32 minutes, title "Reading and Writing · Module 1"). Draw your passages mostly from the natural sciences (biology, ecology, astronomy, earth science) and history, so they do not overlap with other writers' sets.

Build each test in a python script {GEN}/out/test-psat-<id>.py that writes {GEN}/out/test-psat-<id>.json, adding a few questions at a time and re-running the script, so an interruption loses little; if a script exists, read it and continue. Run `python3 {GEN}/tests.py check psat <id>` until it prints RESULT PASS with no warnings. Then take each test as the student would, question by question, without looking at your key: if you can argue for a second choice, or the key depends on a reading the passage does not force, fix the passage or the choices. Write only {GEN}/out/test-psat-conv.json, {GEN}/out/test-psat-expr.json, {GEN}/out/test-psat-rw1.json and their .py scripts; nothing else under {GEN}/out/ and nothing under /home/user/JuniorYearFlashcardsApp.

When you finish, reply with each test's checker summary line, its question-type counts, and anything you were unsure of. Nothing else.

psat-cards:
You are writing the flashcards for a PSAT/NMSQT prep course for one strong student. Read {GEN}/SPEC-psat.md in full — it is the brief: who the student is (790 Math, 730 Reading and Writing on the September SAT, aiming at a 228 Selection Index on the October PSAT/NMSQT), the format you imitate, the file shapes and the checks. Read the math house style in {GEN}/SPEC.md ("Exclusions, borrowing, style": the Unicode-first rule and the only TeX allowed) and the checker {GEN}/tests.py (check_psat).

Write the six unit files {GEN}/out/psat-plan.json, psat-craft.json, psat-info.json, psat-conv.json, psat-expr.json and psat-math.json in the "Cards" shape of the spec, then run `python3 {GEN}/psat_cards.py check <unit>` on each until it prints RESULT PASS. Counts: plan 15 to 25 cards; each other unit 35 to 60, at least 4 per topic (math: at least 6 per topic).

What each unit is for:
- plan: the Selection Index arithmetic (with this student's numbers: 730 and 790 give about 2×73 + 76 = 222; each 10 RW points is 2 index points; 760 RW makes 228), why Reading and Writing is where the points are, how the two-module adaptive test works and why a strong first module matters, pacing (about 71 seconds a Reading and Writing question, about 95 seconds a math question), flag-and-return, when to guess (no penalty), what to do the week before and the morning of. Where a figure is not certain (state cutoffs vary by state and year; commended and semifinalist cutoffs have recently run from about 207 to about 225), say it as a range and say it varies, never a precise number you are unsure of.
- craft, info, conv, expr: the rules, moves and traps that decide the hardest questions of each type, each card testing the move on a FRESH short example (a sentence to fix, a two-sentence passage with a blank, a claim and two findings). Conventions: every boundary rule the SAT tests (independent clauses and what may join them; colons and dashes; nonessential elements and their paired punctuation; lists, including lists with internal commas; no comma between subject and verb, verb and object, or before a restrictive clause; possessives and plural possessives; its/it's-style pairs; subject-verb agreement across long interrupters, inverted order and collective nouns; pronoun-antecedent number; verb tense and aspect from a time cue; dangling and misplaced modifiers; parallel structure). Expression: every transition's logical relation (contrast, concession, cause, example, addition, sequence, emphasis, similarity) with the near-misses that trip strong students (however vs therefore after a concession, for instance vs in addition, similarly vs likewise vs moreover); rhetorical synthesis as goal-matching (the goal words decide: emphasize a difference, introduce to an audience unfamiliar with, present the aim and method). Craft: words in context (secondary meanings of common words: "check", "command", "qualify", "grave", "appreciate"; charge and precision), text structure and purpose (the verb of the choice must match: describes vs argues vs challenges), cross-text (what Text 2's author would say about Text 1's claim, when they partly agree). Info: central idea vs a detail, the finding that would "most directly support" (it must match the specific claim, with the right direction and scope), quantitative evidence (every word of the choice must be true of the table AND serve the claim), inferences (the choice that must be true, not the one that could be).
- math: the careless-miss catalogue for a 790 scorer (the quantity asked for, units, extraneous roots, "must be true" vs "could be true", percent of a changing base, strict vs non-strict inequalities, reading a table's totals, a scatterplot's line of best fit vs the data, SPR entry rules including the digits-that-fit rule and no mixed numbers), and Desmos moves (regression with ~, sliders, intersecting graphs to solve, finding a vertex or max, systems) with their traps. Each card a fresh problem.

Cards are short: q at most 900 characters, a at most 600, a hint of the answer's shape in h, the trap in n. Mark about a quarter c: 1 (the highest-yield). Put accepted short answers in x when the answer is a single word, number or letter. Write only those six files (and any .py helper under {GEN}/out/ named psat-*.py); nothing else under {GEN}/out/ and nothing under /home/user/JuniorYearFlashcardsApp.

When you finish, reply with the checker line for each unit and anything you were unsure of. Nothing else.
